scope: From the seat of the young person turning 18: the moment an age is attained (s 4), when full age and full capacity begin, including the s 5(1)(b) transitional limb (s 5(1)), whether one is an adult in law on a given day, how 'full age', 'adult', 'infant', 'minor' and like words in other laws and instruments are read, with the exclusions for ages in years, pre-commencement instruments and wills, non-WA laws and employment instruments (s 5(2), (3), (5), (7)), and incapacities not due to age (s 5(4)). Transitional s 5(6), (8)-(11) and machinery out.
lives: chloe c025 (2021-03-14): turns 18 -- when, in law, do I come of full age, and am I an adult today but not yesterday

roles: I am the young person, asking about my own age
I am a parent, guardian, trustee or other person dealing with a young person

situation_parameters.name: a law or document I am asking about uses a word like "minor" or "adult"
questions: How is a word like minor or adult read in this law or document

situation_parameters.name: someone is said to lack the legal capacity to do something
questions: Does my coming of full age remove this incapacity of mine
Does the young person's coming of full age remove this incapacity of theirs
